Psychological readings

Philosophical readings · Engineering readings

Psychological modeling organizes changes in feeling, understanding, action, and relationship into explanations that can be questioned and revised. It may begin with relations expressed in ordinary language and progressively specify variables, states, rules, or programs. It may also return from a formal model to experience and discover what the initial account omitted. Its purpose is to understand actual processes and propose consequences that can be compared with new material.

Three connected questions organize these books and papers: psychological process modeling and empirical assessment form the main thread; mind, psychological theories, and philosophical foundations help specify objects and explanatory relations; belief, reasoning, and interaction research contribute local models and methods. They can be read together rather than as three consecutive courses. Links lead to public originals, author resources, or publisher records; a book record does not imply free full text.

Psychological process modeling and empirical assessment

Begin with Guest–Martin and Borsboom and colleagues on making theories explicit, then use the research-methods textbook and Wilson–Collins to examine relations between models and evidence. For extended computational examples, turn to Farrell–Lewandowsky.

Book or paper Where to begin and what it contributes
Guest and Martin (2021), How Computational Modeling Can Force Theory Building in Psychological Science Relations among theory, formal specification, and program implementation. Identify assumptions introduced during modeling and how they can develop the theory in return.
Borsboom et al. (2021), Theory Construction Methodology A proposal connecting phenomena, explanation, formal models, and assessment. Its distinctions can support work in which formalization and empirical inquiry move back and forth.
Jhangiani et al., Research Methods in Psychology, 4th edition Open textbook. Start with measurement, reliability and validity, experimental and nonexperimental designs, and single-subject research; distinguish observed changes from explanations of them.
Wilson and Collins (2019), Ten Simple Rules for the Computational Modeling of Behavioral Data Open paper and code. Simulation, parameter recovery, model recovery, and prediction checks help establish whether data can distinguish candidate models. Good fit alone does not establish a mechanism.
Farrell and Lewandowsky, Computational Modeling of Cognition and Behavior Publisher's first-chapter excerpt; author code connects computational models, estimation, and model comparison. Begin by implementing a small model.

Read here about why experimental designs and measurements can answer a question. For programming, recording, and reproducing an experiment, continue to engineering readings. The same experiment needs both contributions; successful execution and a supported explanation are different outcomes.

Mind, psychological theories, and philosophical foundations

This part includes cognitive explanation, psychoanalysis, and trauma and relational experience. They propose different objects, arguments, and kinds of evidence. Select concepts that help the current question, then compare them with the original text and actual material.

Book or source Reading purpose
Marr, Vision, chapter 1 Distinguish computational task, representation and algorithm, and physical implementation. This framework for vision can help formulate cross-level questions, but its transfer to other psychological phenomena needs explanation.
Probabilistic Models of Cognition The authors' online textbook source repository. Begin with generative models, conditioning, and inference to examine how a cognitive explanation becomes executable; its assumptions remain subject to empirical assessment.
McWilliams, Psychoanalytic Diagnosis, 2nd edition Publisher record. Study how psychoanalysis organizes clinical explanations of personality, defenses, and relationship through concepts and cases, rather than directly assigning categories to an unfamiliar person.
Herman, Trauma and Recovery Publisher record. Read trauma, relationship, and recovery in social context, attending to the different contributions of narrative, theoretical explanation, and research evidence.
Walker, Complex PTSD: From Surviving to Thriving Author's book and excerpt entrance. Read emotional flashbacks, self-criticism, and relational experience; compare this clinical and self-help framework with other research.
Freud and Lacan's original-text entrances The philosophy page retains thinkers, texts, and their intellectual contribution to this collection. Psychological reading asks how their concepts interpret experience, speech, and relationship, and which explanations need cases or further evidence.

Psychoanalysis has philosophical connections as well as psychological and clinical traditions; its appearance on the philosophy page does not exclude it from psychological reading. For philosophical questions about knowledge, explanation, and mind, continue to philosophical readings. Understanding a particular person requires their actual experience and revisable modeling.

Belief, reasoning, and interaction research

This part connects how explanations should be updated with how participants actually change in interaction. Logic describes relations under rules; psychological research investigates actual processes. Each can inform the other without replacing its evidence.

Paper or reference Reading purpose
Logic of Belief Revision Use AGM and related frameworks to distinguish expansion, contraction, and revision, while keeping formal rationality distinct from a person's actual changes.
Dynamic Epistemic Logic Compare information events, knowledge and belief states, and updates; public announcements do not represent every actual interaction.
De Jaegher and Di Paolo (2007), Participatory Sense-Making Include interaction, coordination, and sense-making in an explanation; ask what separate descriptions of participants' internal states might omit.
Fonagy and Allison (2014), The Role of Mentalizing and Epistemic Trust in the Therapeutic Relationship Institutional manuscript entrance. Connect understanding mental states, epistemic trust, and social learning; this is a particular theoretical argument, not proof that every interaction is effective.

These resources make psychological modeling a learnable practice: propose explanations, specify relations, seek discriminating material, and revise through interaction and outcomes. They connect with philosophical understanding and engineering realization in Trinity.
